what_this_is: The DECLARATION behind /registry/doors.html. It names this estate's four ladders, their rungs, and — the load-bearing part — the DOOR on each: the condition the next rung will not accept work without. It contains NO COUNTS. Every count on the page is computed at build time by admin/build/gen_doors.py from registry/ and packs/, and a door whose computed state disagrees with the `expect` below FAILS THE BUILD — in either direction. A door opening is news, and news that does not interrupt anybody is news nobody reads.
ported_from: newsroom.sgit.ai/briefs/10__the-newsroom-floor.md §8, CC BY 4.0 — the state map, not the room. See briefs/v0.33.65.
how_to_change_a_door: Do not edit the count; there isn't one. If a door has genuinely opened, change its `expect` to "open" in the same commit that says so, and the build passes again.

ladders.label: The bootstrap gradient
ladders.asks: How far can an agent get from nothing?
ladders.source: pki.sgit.ai/bootstrap/index.html — the site's own three steps

rungs.label: controls a private key
rungs.means: Free. Proves possession, and nothing else.

rungs.label: …whose private half is scarce
rungs.means: A signature's value is the scarcity of the private half.

door.condition: a keypair whose private half has a durable home

rungs.label: recognised by the project
rungs.means: A policy decision, not a computation — today a git commit reviewed by a human.

rungs.label: …via the designed append lane
rungs.means: The account-less narrow door the whole bootstrap argument rests on.

door.condition: an append lane that accepts a token holder with no account
door.why: the lane is unbuilt; the readiness report's Q2 — whether a lane with no anchors accepts any token holder — is unanswered, and one experiment would answer it

rungs.label: delegated an accepted mandate
rungs.means: Scoped, dated, revocable.

rungs.label: …on a non-fixture authority
rungs.means: An issuer whose private half is not published.

door.condition: an issuer key that anybody cannot forge
door.why: every mandate in this register is signed by the fixture root, whose private half is published in this repository

ladders.label: The tier ladder
ladders.asks: How strong is a control, and who enforces it?
ladders.source: packs/grant-and-mandate/src/01__concepts.md — a control bounds a grant only when it is enforced by something the grant does not include

rungs.label: no control at all
rungs.means: An absence, stated.

rungs.label: expectation
rungs.means: Written in a prompt or a policy file. It is a mandate, and a mandate is not a control.

rungs.label: setting
rungs.means: Enforced by the tool itself, inside the grant. Bypassable by anything running as that grant.

door.condition: it must be enforced outside the grant it bounds

rungs.label: boundary, observed
rungs.means: Enforced by something outside the grant. Observed in somebody else's product, not built here.

rungs.label: boundary, built by this estate
rungs.means: The same allow-list evaluated where the agent cannot reach it.

door.condition: an enforcement point outside the grant — branch protection, or a required CI check
door.why: the only enforcement point built here is a pre-push hook, which sits inside the grant it bounds; reaching boundary is a change of location, not of policy

ladders.label: The ordering rule
ladders.asks: How far along the chain has anything actually travelled?
ladders.source: packs/grant-and-mandate/src/01__concepts.md — reality → twin → facts → finding → risks → decisions

rungs.label: twin — environments measured
rungs.means: The installation every fact attaches to.

rungs.label: facts — grants
rungs.means: Measured, dated, provenance per node.

rungs.label: …signed, with a subject identity
rungs.means: A fact needs a stater to be weighable.

door.condition: a grant signed by a named measurer, about a keyed environment
door.why: both library entries are unsigned JSON outside the register, and their subject is a filename rather than an identity — v0.33.64 §4.2

rungs.label: finding — excess authority
rungs.means: grant − mandate. The exposure nobody accepted.

rungs.label: finding — shortfall
rungs.means: mandate − grant. The operations direction, and where the next over-broad credential comes from.

door.condition: a capability vocabulary, so the mandate can be enumerated against real names
door.why: the shortfall column in the rendered delta block is a hardcoded string; what a capability name IS remains the estate's largest open question

rungs.label: finding — blind spots
rungs.means: library − self-report. The only thing that makes a self-report falsifiable.

door.condition: two agents measuring against a common reference
door.why: there are two library entries and one agent; the three-term block renders its middle column empty on purpose

rungs.label: decisions — with a named acceptor
rungs.means: A separate node: named acceptor, interval.

door.condition: somebody willing to put their name against an exposure
door.why: acceptor is null on every excess row, by construction — excess authority is unaccepted by definition, and nobody has accepted any of it since

ladders.label: The confidence ladder
ladders.asks: How much can any of this bear?
ladders.source: graphs.sgit.ai — the confidence ladder, adopted for this estate in brief v0.33.64

rungs.label: an attributable edge
rungs.means: A signed statement. PKI's contribution: not trust, but attribution.

rungs.label: an independent measurement
rungs.means: Weight by independence, not by count — ten citations of one source are one source.

door.condition: a measurement taken from outside the environment being measured
door.why: both library entries record that the instrument IS the subject, so every path in this register terminates in one origin

rungs.label: a registry pointing at a registry
rungs.means: Recursion: zoom into any node and it expands under identical rules.

door.condition: a second registry, run by somebody else
door.why: the fractal claim is falsifiable and untestable with one instance — v0.33.64 §2
